title: What happened in AI — Aug 31, 2026
intro: A coding agent silently deleted 92% of the AI nodes in n8n's most-cited workflow dataset, and a same-day guardrail tool promised deterministic sub-microsecond execution limits meant to catch exactly that kind of failure. Two new open-source orchestrators and a wave of MCP tooling reinforced that production agents are increasingly run as supervised background jobs, not simple prompt loops.
Separately, a free DeepSeek-based coding harness is being pitched as a substitute for paid Claude Code subscriptions, while Zhipu and peer Chinese labs reported sharp revenue and call-volume growth.
highlights: A coding agent erased 92% of AI nodes in n8n's most-cited dataset, with no audit trail catching it until after the fact.
VajraClaw shipped a deterministic <1µs execution guardrail for agents, launched the same day as the n8n incident writeup.
Keel and Intent, two new open-source agent orchestrators, both frame production agents as supervised jobs rather than prompt loops.
A free DeepSeek-based coding harness is being pitched as a substitute for paid Claude Code subscriptions.
Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash topped global AI call volume as China led total call volume for an 18th straight week.
AWS was named a Leader in Forrester's Q4 2025 AI Infrastructure Wave, the highest strategy score among 13 providers.
